props.caption: Godot 4.7 documentation · Shading language · captured at build time

B11.visual_intent: The real Godot 4.7 shading-language page in a browser window; the camera pushes in on the sentence that says it is similar to GLSL ES 3.0 and a terracotta ring marks it.
B11.motion_claim: The camera pushes in on the sentence the voice is describing.

show.event: push-in + ring on the GLSL sentence

B11.runner_up: manim: GDScript line beside a shader line
B11.why: The language claim is a documentation claim; the documentation itself is the evidence (SHOW-THE-THING).

B09.visual_intent: Act title 'Setting Up a Shader' (serif 40) top-left. Three boxes slide in left to right and link: 'a node (Sprite2D, ColorRect…)' → 'ShaderMaterial' → 'your shader (.gdshader file)'. A small dot travels from the shader back to the node.
B09.motion_claim: Each box slides in as it is named; the dot travels back to the node, meaning 'look'.
B09.why: Three nested things is a structure with a shape; a drawn chain with a travelling dot is clearer than prose.

B10.capture_spec: E1: four real editor states recorded by the editor driver (editor-capture/README.md): Material empty; Shader Material in the slot (menu: heading New, then ShaderMaterial); a Shader added (New Shader..., Create Shader dialog, mode Canvas Item); the shader editor open in the bottom panel. Scripted editor session; the clicks themselves are not shown.
B10.visual_intent: Four real frames of the Godot editor's Inspector for a Sprite2D, one per state: Material empty; ShaderMaterial added; a Shader added; the shader editor open. Slow cross-dissolves between them; a terracotta ring on the slot being named.
B10.motion_claim: The ring moves slot to slot as the voice names each click.
B10.why: Real editor frames are the rung-1 SHOW-THE-THING answer; the reconstruction is the labelled fallback.

B12.visual_intent: Left: the line `shader_type canvas_item;` over a flat teal sprite icon. Right: `shader_type spatial;` over a small isometric cube. Three small tiles fade in underneath: particles, sky, fog.
B12.motion_claim: The two first lines type in, each over its picture, then the three small tiles arrive.
B12.why: Two worlds side by side, each with its own first line, is the contrast the sentence names.
